ground_truth.reason: The vulnerable authlib.jose.rfc7515.jws.JsonWebSignature serialize and deserialize methods belong to Authlib's JOSE signing subsystem, which this project pulls in only transitively through FastMCP. The sole consumer of authlib.jose is FastMCP's JWTVerifier, and the project constructs its FastMCP server with no authentication configured, so JWTVerifier is never created. Because nothing else references authlib.jose, JsonWebSignature.serialize_compact, deserialize_compact and the related JSON methods are never invoked, and no valid call path to any of the vulnerable functions exists.

The vulnerable _publish, _listen and _thread methods belong to python-socketio's external message-queue managers (the AioPika, Redis, Kafka and generic PubSub backends), which the project pulls in only transitively through Chainlit. Chainlit instantiates socketio.AsyncServer in ASGI mode with no client_manager argument, so it falls back to the default in-process AsyncManager. None of the message-queue manager classes are ever constructed, so no valid call path to any of the vulnerable functions exists.

The vulnerable authlib.jose.rfc7515.jws.JsonWebSignature.deserialize_compact and the authlib.jose.util.extract_header and extract_segment helpers belong to Authlib's JWS deserialization path, which is reachable only through FastMCP's JWTVerifier. The project never configures MCP authentication, so JWTVerifier is never instantiated and no JWS deserialization is performed. No valid call path to any of the vulnerable functions exists.

The vulnerable authlib.jose.rfc7518.jwe_zips.DeflateZipAlgorithm.decompress method belongs to Authlib's JWE decompression handling, and Authlib is imported only by FastMCP's JWT provider when JWT authentication is configured. This project builds its FastMCP server with no authentication, so no JWE or JWS decoding is ever performed. No valid call path to the vulnerable function exists.

The vulnerable starlette.responses.FileResponse._parse_range_header parses the Range header when Starlette streams a file response. This project registers its own StaticCacheMiddleware, whose _create_file_response returns a Starlette FileResponse for requests under /assets/ and /static/, and Chainlit likewise serves /assets through FileResponse. Since FileResponse.__call__ invokes _parse_range_header on any incoming Range header, the vulnerable function is reached on every ranged request for a static asset.

The vulnerable create_callback_html and the fastmcp.utilities.ui page-building helpers belong to FastMCP's client-side OAuth callback rendering, reached only through the client OAuth provider; the named fastmcp.utilities.ui.create_detail_box does not even exist in the installed 2.11.3. This project uses FastMCP only as a server and builds its HTTP app that way, never importing fastmcp.Client or its OAuth flow. The client OAuth callback path is never entered, so no valid call path to the vulnerable functions exists.

The vulnerable fastmcp.cli.install.shared.process_common_args is invoked only by the fastmcp install subcommands. This project never runs the FastMCP command-line interface; it ships its own Typer-based CLI and drives FastMCP programmatically. Because the install subcommands are never entered, no valid call path to the vulnerable function exists.

The vulnerable werkzeug.security.safe_join is called only by Werkzeug's send_from_directory helper and its SharedDataMiddleware, and Werkzeug enters this project only transitively through openapi-core under FastMCP. The application serves files through Starlette, FastAPI and Chainlit and never imports Werkzeug or uses its file-serving utilities. No valid call path to the vulnerable function exists.

The vulnerable FastMCP.__init__ belongs to the MCP SDK's mcp.server.fastmcp.server module. This project imports the separate third-party fastmcp 2.x package, whose FastMCP class is built on mcp.server.lowlevel and is not the SDK's FastMCP; the SDK class is referenced only by fastmcp's CLI, client and inspect tooling, none of which lie on the application's path. From the MCP SDK the project uses only ClientSession, so the vulnerable constructor is never invoked and no valid call path exists.

The vulnerable urllib3.response.MultiDecoder.__init__ is constructed when urllib3 decodes a response body carrying a comma-separated Content-Encoding. The claimed path routing this constructor through requests.adapters.BaseAdapter.__init__ is a fabricated edge, since that abstract initializer does not build urllib3 response objects, but the vulnerable function is genuinely reached through the real chain. The project's check_url_status calls requests.get with the default stream=False, so requests reads the body and urllib3's HTTPResponse.read runs _init_decoder, which returns a MultiDecoder whenever multiple stacked encodings are present, so the vulnerable function is reached on any such response.

The vulnerable urllib3.response.GzipDecoder.decompress and DeflateDecoder.decompress run when urllib3 decodes a gzip- or deflate-encoded response body, and urllib3 enters the project transitively through requests. The project's check_url_status calls requests.get with the default stream=False and reads the response content, which drives urllib3's HTTPResponse.read into _init_decoder and the matching decoder's decompress method whenever the response carries a gzip or deflate Content-Encoding. The vulnerable function is therefore reached on any compressed response the project fetches.

The vulnerable filelock._unix._acquire and filelock._windows._acquire back FileLock.acquire, which Hugging Face Hub enters through its WeakFileLock only along model-download paths; filelock reaches this project transitively through litellm, tokenizers and huggingface-hub. The project performs only remote-API chat via litellm.acompletion and never downloads Hugging Face models, so FileLock.acquire and the underlying _acquire are never invoked. The vulnerable 3.19.1 was unavailable and the identical 3.20.0 was analyzed, and no valid call path to the vulnerable functions exists.

The vulnerable FrameworkIntegration.get_state_data and its sibling session-state methods belong to authlib.integrations.base_client, Authlib's OAuth client integration layer. Within FastMCP only authlib.jose is imported, never base_client, and the project configures no Authlib OAuth client of its own. No valid call path to any of the vulnerable functions exists.

The vulnerable marshmallow.error_store.merge_errors and ErrorStore.store_error fire only during a marshmallow Schema.load or validate, which dataclasses-json triggers exclusively through its .schema() API; marshmallow reaches the project transitively through dataclasses-json under Chainlit. Chainlit serializes only through dataclasses-json's pure-Python to_dict and from_dict helpers and never calls .schema(), so Schema.load is never invoked. No valid call path to the vulnerable functions exists.

The vulnerable chainlit.socket.connect is Chainlit's Socket.IO connect handler. This project mounts the full Chainlit server, loading its application module and copying all of Chainlit's routes, including the Socket.IO ASGI app at /ws/socket.io. The handler fires on every WebSocket connection and, with authentication left at its default enabled setting, invokes _authenticate_connection, so the vulnerable function is reached on every incoming WebSocket connection.

The vulnerable aiohttp.compression_utils.ZLibDecompressor.decompress_sync and decompress run on the client response path: when a response carries a Content-Encoding header, aiohttp's DeflateBuffer feeds data through decompress_sync, and that DeflateBuffer is created during client request/response handling because auto_decompress defaults to True. The project uses aiohttp as an HTTP client and reads every response through read, json or text, and this pure-Python decompressor is not shadowed by a C extension. The vulnerable function is therefore reached whenever a server returns a compressed response body.

The vulnerable aiohttp.http_parser.HttpRequestParser._is_chunked_te and the HttpParser.parse_headers header handling belong to aiohttp's HTTP request-parsing pipeline, which is exercised only by an aiohttp.web server; this project runs no aiohttp.web server. In addition, the pure-Python parser is shadowed by aiohttp's compiled C extension (the _http_parser.pyd is present), so even client response parsing runs in C rather than this code. The vulnerable functions are reachable only when aiohttp is forced to its pure-Python parser under AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS, which the default installation does not use.

The vulnerable aiohttp.web_request.BaseRequest.http_range belongs to aiohttp's web-server request API. This project serves its HTTP application with Uvicorn and Starlette through FastMCP and uses aiohttp only as a client, never constructing a BaseRequest. No valid call path to the vulnerable function exists.

The vulnerable aiohttp.web_urldispatcher.StaticResource.resolve and StaticResource._handle belong to aiohttp's web-server router for static resources. This project runs no aiohttp.web server and registers no aiohttp static resources. No valid call path to the vulnerable functions exists.

The vulnerable aiohttp.multipart.BodyPartReader.read_chunk, its _read_chunk_from_stream helper and aiohttp.web_request.BaseRequest.post are all server-side multipart and form handling. This project uses aiohttp only as a client, reading responses through read, text and json, and never constructs a MultipartReader or calls request.post. No valid call path to the vulnerable functions exists.

The vulnerable aiohttp.web_request.BaseRequest.post is aiohttp's web-server form parser. This project runs no aiohttp.web server and uses aiohttp only as a client, so BaseRequest.post is never reached. No valid call path to the vulnerable function exists.

The vulnerable aiohttp.streams.StreamReader is the client response body reader: aiohttp's ResponseHandler holds a StreamReader as the response payload. Because this project uses aiohttp as a client and reads every response through read, json or text, StreamReader.__init__ runs on each response, end_http_chunk_receiving fires for chunked responses and _read_nowait_chunk is driven by read; the class is pure-Python and not shadowed by a C extension. The vulnerable functions are therefore reached on every response the project reads.

The vulnerable aiohttp._cookie_helpers.parse_cookie_header is called by ClientRequest.update_cookies only when a Cookie header is already present on the outgoing request. This project passes cookies as a dict to ClientSession, which only writes the Cookie header and never parses an existing one, so the gating condition is never met. No valid call path to the vulnerable function exists.

The vulnerable protobuf json_format._Parser._ConvertAnyMessage is reachable only through json_format.Parse or ParseDict, and protobuf reaches the project transitively through Chainlit's telemetry chain of literalai, traceloop and the OTLP exporter. The OTLP exporters serialize with the binary SerializeToString rather than JSON, no json_format use exists outside protobuf itself, and the application imports neither protobuf nor OpenTelemetry directly. With no JSON-to-Any conversion path, confirmed against protobuf 6.32.0, no valid call path to the vulnerable function exists.

The vulnerable urllib3.response.HTTPResponse.drain_conn is called only inside urllib3's connectionpool.urlopen, in its redirect branch gated on redirect=True and its retry branch gated on the retry policy. The requests library, through which the project reaches urllib3, calls urlopen with redirect=False and a zero-retry policy, so both branches are disabled, and the project only issues plain requests.get and requests.post calls. No valid call path to the vulnerable function exists.

The vulnerable werkzeug.security.safe_join, the same function as in the earlier Werkzeug finding, has only two callers, send_from_directory and SharedDataMiddleware, neither of which lies on the application's path. Werkzeug enters the project only transitively through openapi-core and is never imported by the application. No valid call path to the vulnerable function exists.

The vulnerable filelock._soft._acquire backs SoftFileLock, whose only consumer is huggingface_hub's WeakFileLock fallback, entered exclusively during Hugging Face downloads. The project performs remote-API chat and never triggers a Hugging Face download, so SoftFileLock and its _acquire are never used. The analysis substituted the identical 3.20.0 for the unavailable 3.19.1, and no valid call path to the vulnerable function exists.

The vulnerable pure-Python aiohttp.http_parser.HttpParser.__init__ and HeadersParser.parse_headers are shadowed by aiohttp's compiled C extension (the _http_parser.pyd is present), so client response parsing runs in C rather than this code. The claimed path routing these functions through requests.adapters.BaseAdapter.__init__ is fabricated, since requests does not delegate parsing to aiohttp. The vulnerable functions are reachable only when aiohttp is forced to its pure-Python parser under AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS, which the default installation does not use.

The vulnerable python_multipart.multipart.File.__init__ is instantiated only by python-multipart's high-level FormParser; python-multipart reaches the project transitively through Chainlit and the MCP SDK, and the relevant trigger would be Starlette form parsing at POST /upload. Starlette drives the low-level MultipartParser with its own callbacks and UploadFile and never constructs a python-multipart File. The claimed path routing File.__init__ through requests.adapters.BaseAdapter.__init__ is fabricated, since requests does not construct python-multipart objects, so no valid call path to the vulnerable function exists.

The vulnerable requests.utils.extract_zipped_paths is called from HTTPAdapter's cert_verify during a requests call. The project depends on requests directly, and both its check_url_status and its file-upload helper issue requests.get calls, which flow through Session.send and HTTPAdapter.send into cert_verify. The vulnerable function is therefore reached on the certificate-verification step of every request the project issues through requests.

The vulnerable werkzeug.security.safe_join, the same function as in the earlier Werkzeug findings, is reachable only through send_from_directory or SharedDataMiddleware, and the application calls neither. Werkzeug is present only as a transitive dependency and is never imported by the application. No valid call path to the vulnerable function exists.

The vulnerable authlib.jose.rfc7515.jws.JsonWebSignature._prepare_algorithm_key and authlib.jose.rfc7516.jwe.prepare_key belong to Authlib's JOSE key-preparation path, reachable only through FastMCP's JWTVerifier. The project builds its FastMCP server with no authentication, so JWTVerifier is never created and the key-preparation path is never entered. No valid call path to the vulnerable functions exists.

The vulnerable authlib.oidc.core.claims._verify_hash performs the OIDC ID-token hash check and runs only inside FastMCP's JWTVerifier, the sole route by which Authlib is reached. The project builds its FastMCP server with no authentication and never uses Authlib directly, so the OIDC claims validation is never entered. No valid call path to the vulnerable function exists.

The vulnerable functions are dotenv.main.rewrite together with its callers dotenv.main.set_key and dotenv.main.unset_key, which write changes back into a .env file. This project only calls dotenv.main.load_dotenv, whose load_dotenv-to-set_as_environment_variables read path never invokes rewrite, and it never calls set_key or unset_key. The tool's reachable trace followed the read path rather than the write path where the vulnerable functions live, so no valid call path to any of them exists.

The vulnerable function authlib.jose.rfc7518.jws_algs.NoneAlgorithm.verify runs only during the JWT verification performed by fastmcp's JWTVerifier. This project never enables MCP authentication, so no token verification runs and the vulnerable function is never reached.

The vulnerable function fastmcp.utilities.openapi.director.RequestDirector._build_url belongs to RequestDirector, which is imported only inside FastMCPOpenAPI and constructed solely through FastMCP.from_openapi or FastMCP.from_fastapi. This project builds its server with a plain FastMCP instance, @mcp.tool decorators, and http_app, and never calls from_openapi or from_fastapi. RequestDirector is therefore never constructed and no valid call path exists.

The vulnerable functions aiohttp.connector._DNSCacheTable.__init__ and _DNSCacheTable.add are reached when a ClientSession is created without an explicit connector: the session builds a default TCPConnector, which constructs a _DNSCacheTable, and add runs as DNS resolutions are cached. This project creates a ClientSession without a connector and issues real requests, so both __init__ and add execute. The tool's claimed path routing requests.adapters.BaseAdapter.__init__ into aiohttp.connector._DNSCacheTable is a fabricated cross-library edge, but the vulnerable functions are genuinely reached through aiohttp's own connector on every request.

The vulnerable function aiohttp.formdata.FormData.add_field is called directly by this project, which constructs a FormData and calls add_field in both its ComfyUI base executor and its RunningHub client before posting the form through session.post or session.request. The vulnerable function sits on this exact path, so it is reached whenever those uploads run.

The vulnerable function aiohttp.web_urldispatcher.StaticResource._handle is the static file handler of an aiohttp.web server. This project runs no aiohttp.web server and registers no aiohttp routes, so the handler is never dispatched and no valid call path exists.

The vulnerable functions are aiohttp.multipart.MultipartReader.__init__, MultipartReader._read_headers, and aiohttp.streams.StreamReader.readuntil, where readuntil is reached only through MultipartReader._read_headers or through StreamReader.readline. This project never consumes multipart responses and instead reads bodies with read, readany, json, and text, none of which call readuntil, so no valid call path to any of the vulnerable functions exists.

The vulnerable function aiohttp.web_request.BaseRequest.post is the server-side request body parser. This project uses aiohttp only as a client and runs no aiohttp.web server, so BaseRequest.post is never reached and no valid call path exists.

The vulnerable function aiohttp.client.ClientSession._request is the core dispatch through which every get, post, and request call funnels. This project issues session.get, session.post, and session.request in its ComfyUI base executor and RunningHub client, so _request is unavoidably executed on every one of those calls.

The vulnerable functions are aiohttp.web_response.StreamResponse._set_status, which together with the aiohttp.web HTTPException constructor belongs to the unused server side, and aiohttp.http_writer._py_serialize_headers, which is shadowed by the compiled C _serialize_headers since _http_writer.pyd is installed. This project runs no aiohttp.web server and uses the compiled writer, so neither is reachable. The tool's claimed path routing requests.adapters.BaseAdapter.__init__ into aiohttp.web_exception is a fabricated cross-library edge and does not represent a real call chain.

The vulnerable functions aiohttp.http_parser.HeadersParser.parse_headers and HttpParser.parse_headers are the pure-Python header parsers, which are shadowed by the compiled C extension because _http_parser.pyd is installed. Client-side header parsing therefore runs in C, so the vulnerable functions are reachable only when the application runs with AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS set, since the default installation replaces the pure-Python parser with the compiled C extension.

The vulnerable functions aiohttp.cookiejar.CookieJar.save and CookieJar.load provide on-disk cookie persistence. This project never calls save or load and only passes a cookies dictionary to ClientSession, which routes through update_cookies and filter_cookies instead, so no valid call path to the vulnerable functions exists.

The vulnerable function PIL.FitsImagePlugin.decode is dispatched by PIL.Image.open according to image content, with FITS magic bytes routing to the FITS decoder. This project opens downloaded image content with Image.open and then calls crop, which forces a full load and decode, so a FITS-format input reaches the vulnerable function. Confidence is medium because the pillow 11.3.0 source is absent from the dependency snapshot.

The vulnerable function authlib.oauth2.rfc6749.authorization_server.AuthorizationServer.get_authorization_grant belongs to authlib's OAuth2 authorization server. The only authlib code this project touches is authlib.jose by way of fastmcp, and it never imports authlib.oauth2 or runs an OAuth2 server, so no valid call path exists.

The vulnerable function PIL.PdfParser.read_prev_trailer runs only when reading or appending to an existing PDF, and because the PDF plugin registers only a save handler, Image.open cannot route to it. This project never reads or writes PDFs and saves only JPEG output, so the vulnerable function is never reached. Confidence is medium because the pillow source is absent from the dependency snapshot.

The vulnerable function PIL.ImageFile.setimage is part of the core file-decode machinery invoked through ImageFile.load. This project opens arbitrary downloaded images with Image.open and calls crop, which forces the load that drives the decoder's setimage, so the vulnerable function is reached on the general open-and-load route. Confidence is medium because the pillow source is absent from the dependency snapshot.

The vulnerable functions litellm.proxy.management_endpoints.key_management_endpoints._check_allowed_routes_caller_permission and _common_key_generation_helper are route handlers of the standalone LiteLLM Proxy server. This project uses litellm only as a client through litellm.acompletion and never imports litellm.proxy or runs the proxy server, so no valid call path to the vulnerable functions exists.

The vulnerable function aiohttp.client.ClientSession._request is the mandatory dispatch point for all client requests, the same function noted for S0042. This project makes client requests through session.get, session.post, and session.request, every one of which passes through _request, so the vulnerable function is reached on each call.

The vulnerable function jwt.api_jws.PyJWS._load is reached transitively through chainlit, which this project mounts with authentication enabled by way of a password auth callback. Chainlit's JWT handling calls jwt.decode from get_current_user, and decode flows through decode_complete and api_jws.decode_complete into PyJWS._load, so any authenticated request reaches the vulnerable function.

The vulnerable function starlette.datastructures.URL.__init__ is invoked when starlette's Request.url builds a URL from the request scope. This project registers a static-cache middleware on its FastAPI application that reads request.url.path on every request, so URL.__init__ runs on normal HTTP traffic. The tool's claimed path routing requests.adapters.BaseAdapter.__init__ into starlette.datastructures is a fabricated cross-library edge, but the vulnerable function is genuinely reached through the middleware.

The vulnerable function starlette.staticfiles.get_response requires a mounted starlette StaticFiles ASGI application. StaticFiles appears nowhere in this project, chainlit, fastmcp, or mcp, and chainlit serves static content through FastAPI route handlers that return FileResponse rather than through StaticFiles. Since StaticFiles is never mounted, no valid call path to the vulnerable function exists.

The vulnerable function aiohttp.payload.headers is a property read during multipart FormData serialization, where FormData._gen_form_data accesses each part's headers. This project builds a multipart FormData with add_field and sends it, triggering _gen_form_data and the headers access, so the vulnerable function is reached on that path. Confidence is medium because the exact vulnerable semantics of the CVE are unspecified.

The vulnerable functions PIL.BdfFontFile.bdf_char, PIL.FontFile.compile, and PIL.PcfFontFile.append are bitmap-font parsers reached only through ImageFont.load and never through Image.open, because fonts are not image plugins. This project imports only Image from PIL and uses no ImageFont or ImageDraw, so no valid call path to the vulnerable functions exists.

The vulnerable functions are the same bitmap-font parsers PIL.BdfFontFile.bdf_char, PIL.FontFile.compile, and PIL.PcfFontFile.append as in S0056. This project uses PIL only to open, crop, size, and save JPEG images and never loads fonts, so no reaching chain to the vulnerable functions exists.

The vulnerable functions span aiohttp.web_protocol.__init__, which is server-side and unused, the pure-Python aiohttp.http_parser.__init__, feed_data, and get_content_length, which are shadowed by the compiled C extension since _http_parser.pyd is installed, and aiohttp.base_protocol.resume_reading, a peripheral flow-control method rather than the vulnerable parser. With the default compiled parser in place and no aiohttp.web server running, the vulnerable parsing functions are reachable only when the application runs with AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS set.

The vulnerable functions aiohttp._websocket.reader_py._handle_frame and _feed_data belong to aiohttp's WebSocket reader. This project does not use aiohttp WebSockets; its websocket executor imports the separate websockets package and uses aiohttp only for HTTP POST, and the pure-Python reader_py is in any case shadowed by the compiled reader_c since reader_c.pyd is installed. The vulnerable functions are doubly unreachable.

The vulnerable function aiohttp.client_middleware_digest_auth.__call__ runs only when the digest authentication middleware is attached. This project configures no client middlewares and passes no auth parameter, so the middleware is never instantiated and no valid call path exists.

The vulnerable function aiohttp.streams.StreamReader._read_nowait sits on the client body-read path, where read calls readany, which calls _read_nowait. This project reads every response with read, json, or text, and the function is pure-Python rather than C-shadowed, so the vulnerable function is reached on every response read.

The vulnerable functions aiohttp.cookiejar.CookieJar.save and cookiejar._load_json_data handle cookie-jar persistence. As with S0045, this project never calls save or load and only passes a cookies dictionary, which routes through update_cookies and filter_cookies, so no valid call path to the vulnerable functions exists.

The vulnerable function aiohttp.web_response.write_eof is a response method of an aiohttp.web server. This project runs no aiohttp.web server and never constructs web responses, using aiohttp only as a client, so no valid call path to the vulnerable function exists.

The vulnerable functions are again the bitmap-font parsers PIL.BdfFontFile.bdf_char, PIL.FontFile.compile, and PIL.PcfFontFile.append, which require ImageFont, ImageDraw, or explicit font-file handling. This project uses PIL only to open, crop, and save JPEG images and does none of those, so no valid call path to the vulnerable functions exists.

The vulnerable function PIL.GdImageFile._open handles the libgd .gd format through an explicit-only plugin that is not in the open registry and carries no magic bytes, so it is reached only by calling GdImageFile.open directly. This project only calls Image.open and never imports GdImageFile, so no valid call path to the vulnerable function exists.

The vulnerable function chainlit.socket.restore_existing_session is called unconditionally by chainlit's socket connect handler, which is registered as the socket.io connect event handler. This project copies chainlit's socket.io mount into its FastAPI application, so any WebSocket connection reaches the vulnerable function.

The vulnerable functions litellm.llms.litellm_proxy.skills.prompt_injection.extract_all_files and sandbox_executor.execute belong to litellm's proxy guardrails and skills. This project only calls litellm.acompletion with standard chat parameters and never enables the litellm_proxy skills or sandbox, so no valid call path to the vulnerable functions exists; the litellm source is absent from the dependency snapshot, but the client-only usage is definitive.
No path.

The vulnerable functions belong to aiohttp's HTTP request parsing pipeline. This project serves its FastAPI application with Uvicorn, so incoming requests are parsed by Uvicorn's h11/httptools implementation rather than aiohttp.http_parser. The project does not create or run an aiohttp web server, and no valid call path to any of the vulnerable functions exists.

The vulnerable http_range property belongs to aiohttp.web_request.BaseRequest. This project uses FastAPI and Starlette request objects and serves the application with Uvicorn. It does not create or process aiohttp.web request objects, so no valid call path to BaseRequest.http_range exists.

Although the project serves static files, it uses starlette.staticfiles.StaticFiles rather than aiohttp.web_urldispatcher.StaticResource. The project does not configure an aiohttp web router or create an aiohttp StaticResource, so neither StaticResource.resolve nor StaticResource._handle is reachable.

The project accepts multipart form requests through FastAPI, but those requests are parsed by Starlette's MultiPartParser and python-multipart. The application does not use aiohttp.web_request.BaseRequest or aiohttp.multipart.BodyPartReader, so no valid call path to the vulnerable functions exists.

Multipart form submissions in this project are handled by FastAPI, Starlette, and python-multipart rather than aiohttp.web_request.BaseRequest.post. The project does not run an aiohttp web application or create aiohttp request objects, so the vulnerable function is unreachable.

The reported paths contain invalid cross-library constructor edges. HTTPX's CookieConflict.__init__ and pytest's RaisesExc.__init__ do not create or invoke aiohttp.streams.StreamReader. The vulnerable StreamReader functions are only reached through aiohttp's own HTTP parsing and stream-processing pipeline, while this project serves its FastAPI application with Uvicorn and does not use aiohttp stream objects. No valid call path to any of the vulnerable functions exists.

The vulnerable cookie parser belongs to aiohttp's HTTP request-processing pipeline. The project uses FastAPI, Starlette, and Uvicorn and does not process requests with aiohttp, so no valid call path to aiohttp._cookie_helpers.parse_cookie_header exists.

The vulnerable functions belong to aiohttp's HTTP parser. Incoming requests in this project are parsed by Uvicorn's h11/httptools stack rather than aiohttp.http_parser, and the project does not instantiate an aiohttp HttpParser.

The project accepts form data through FastAPI and Starlette, but Starlette uses python-multipart's callback-based MultipartParser and creates its own UploadFile objects. It does not instantiate python_multipart.multipart.File, so no valid call path to File.__init__ exists.

The project does not call python-dotenv's set_key, unset_key, or rewrite functions. These functions modify dotenv files and are not implicitly invoked merely because python-dotenv is installed, so no valid call path to the vulnerable functions exists.

_DNSCacheTable is created and used by aiohttp's client connector. The project does not instantiate aiohttp.ClientSession, TCPConnector, or _DNSCacheTable, so neither _DNSCacheTable.__init__ nor _DNSCacheTable.add is reachable.

The vulnerable FormData.add_field function belongs to aiohttp's outbound multipart request implementation. The project does not construct aiohttp.FormData or send requests through aiohttp, so no valid call path exists.

The project serves static files with starlette.staticfiles.StaticFiles rather than aiohttp.web_urldispatcher.StaticResource. It does not create an aiohttp static resource, so StaticResource._handle is unreachable.

Multipart requests in this project are processed by Starlette's MultiPartParser and python-multipart, not aiohttp.multipart.MultipartReader or aiohttp.streams.StreamReader. No valid call path to the vulnerable aiohttp functions exists.
The vulnerable BaseRequest.post function belongs to aiohttp.web. This project uses Starlette request objects and Starlette's form parser, and it does not create aiohttp BaseRequest objects.
The vulnerable function belongs to aiohttp's HTTP client. The project does not instantiate aiohttp.ClientSession or call ClientSession._request, so the redirect-handling code is unreachable.

The vulnerable functions belong to aiohttp's HTTP response-writing pipeline. The project returns responses through FastAPI and Starlette and does not create aiohttp StreamResponse objects, so no valid call path exists.

The vulnerable header parsers belong to aiohttp's HTTP parsing pipeline. Requests in this project are parsed by Uvicorn rather than aiohttp, and the project does not instantiate or invoke aiohttp HttpParser or HeadersParser.

The vulnerable functions require explicit use of aiohttp.CookieJar.save or CookieJar.load. The project does not instantiate aiohttp.CookieJar or persist aiohttp cookie jars, so no valid call path to either function exists.
No vulnerable function (VF) identified for this CVE.

The project runs a FastAPI application backed by Starlette with trailing-slash redirects enabled by default. When an attacker sends a request whose trailing slash does not match a registered route, starlette.routing.Router.app constructs a URL from the attacker-controlled ASGI request scope, directly invoking starlette.datastructures.URL.__init__. Therefore, the vulnerable function is reachable through the application's normal request-routing pipeline.

Since the formatter is never invoked while the application runs, the cache-key function is not reachable.

The vulnerable functions are the cookie jar's on-disk persistence routines, which only run when the application explicitly serializes or deserializes cookies to a file path. LedFx creates default client sessions for its outbound requests and never calls the save or load methods, nor does it configure any cookie-jar file. With no persistence call anywhere in the codebase, neither function is reachable.

The vulnerable function is the central dispatch that aiohttp runs for every outbound client request. LedFx acts as an HTTP client in several places, fetching WLED device information and MusicBrainz cover art with session.get and opening a QLC+ control channel with session.ws_connect, all of which funnel through the client request method. Because these outbound requests execute during normal operation, the vulnerable function is reachable.

The vulnerable function is the mDNS listener routine that processes incoming query packets received on the multicast socket. LedFx starts a full asynchronous Zeroconf engine in its mDNS manager to discover network devices, and that engine binds the multicast listener that hands every inbound query to the vulnerable handler, independent of whether LedFx has registered its own services. Since any mDNS query arriving on the local network is dispatched to this handler while the engine runs, the function is reachable, though the exact internal edges could not be fully traced because the zeroconf source was not cached.

The vulnerable function constructs a URL object while a Starlette ASGI application handles an incoming request. Unlike the earlier FastAPI-based projects, LedFx does not use Starlette or FastAPI at all; it serves its entire web interface and REST API through an aiohttp web server. Because no Starlette request-handling code ever runs, the URL constructor is never invoked and the function is unreachable.

The vulnerable function is the response handler of Starlette's StaticFiles ASGI application. LedFx serves its frontend, fonts, modules, and favicon through aiohttp's own static routing rather than Starlette, and it never imports or mounts a Starlette StaticFiles instance. With no Starlette static handler configured anywhere, its response method cannot be reached.

The vulnerable property is read only while aiohttp serializes a request body payload, which happens when a client request is sent with body data such as multipart form fields. Every outbound request LedFx makes is a bodyless GET or a WebSocket connect, and the project never builds a FormData object or passes request body data. Since no client payload is ever serialized, the property is not accessed and the function is unreachable.

The vulnerable functions are Pillow's BDF and PCF bitmap-font parsers, which are only exercised when loading legacy bitmap font files through the font subsystem. LedFx does use Pillow's font module, but exclusively through the TrueType loader, which reads TrueType and OpenType fonts via FreeType and never routes through the BDF or PCF parsers or the bitmap-font compile step. Because the project loads no BDF or PCF bitmap fonts, these parsers are not reached, though confidence is moderate since the Pillow source was not available to trace directly.

The vulnerable functions are the same BDF and PCF bitmap-font parsers, reached only through Pillow's bitmap-font loading path. LedFx loads fonts solely with the TrueType loader and otherwise uses Pillow to open and manipulate images, neither of which invokes the bitmap-font parsers. With no BDF or PCF font loading in the project, the functions remain unreachable, with moderate confidence given the uncached Pillow source.

The vulnerable functions belong to aiohttp's request-handling and parsing pipeline. Unlike the earlier client-only projects, LedFx genuinely runs an aiohttp web server through an application runner and TCP site, so the request-handler protocol object is constructed for every incoming connection and the flow-control resume routine executes on both server and client transports. The pure-Python HTTP parser entry points in this set are shadowed by aiohttp's compiled C parser extension, but because the server-side request handler is instantiated on the live request path, the vulnerable set is reachable.

The vulnerable functions are the pure-Python implementation of aiohttp's WebSocket frame reader. LedFx does drive aiohttp WebSockets on both sides, exposing a server WebSocket endpoint and opening a client WebSocket to a QLC+ controller, so incoming frames are decoded by the WebSocket reader. However, the pure-Python reader is normally shadowed by aiohttp's compiled Cython reader extension and only executes when extensions are disabled; under that condition the frame-handling functions are reached, which is why this is labelled reachable with moderate confidence.

The vulnerable function is the request hook of aiohttp's digest-authentication client middleware, which only runs when a client session is configured with digest auth. LedFx constructs default client sessions with no middleware and no authentication parameters for all of its outbound requests. Since digest authentication is never configured, the middleware is never invoked and the function is unreachable.

The vulnerable function is part of aiohttp's stream reader on the body-reading path. LedFx reads response bodies from its outbound client requests using the JSON and raw read helpers, and its server request handler reads incoming request bodies as JSON or text, both of which pull data through the stream reader's low-level read routine. Because this reader is a pure-Python component that is not shadowed by a compiled extension and body reading happens routinely, the function is reachable.

The vulnerable functions are the cookie jar's disk persistence routines, invoked only when cookies are explicitly written to or read from a file. LedFx uses default client sessions and never persists cookies to disk or provides a cookie-jar file path. With no save or load call in the codebase, neither function is reachable.

The vulnerable function is the aiohttp web-server routine that finalizes an outgoing HTTP response. Unlike the earlier client-only projects, LedFx runs a real aiohttp web server and returns JSON and file responses from its REST API and frontend routes, and the server writes the end of every one of those responses through this method. Because the server completes responses on the live request path, the function is reachable.

The vulnerable functions are Pillow's BDF and PCF bitmap-font parsers and the bitmap-font compile step, reachable only through the bitmap-font loading path. LedFx loads fonts exclusively with the TrueType loader and never handles BDF or PCF bitmap fonts. Since the bitmap-font parsers are never entered, the functions are unreachable, with moderate confidence because the Pillow source was not cached for direct tracing.

The vulnerable function opens libgd .gd images and belongs to an explicit-only Pillow plugin that is not registered in the automatic image-format detection used by the general open call. LedFx opens images only through Pillow's standard open function and never imports or directly invokes the libgd plugin. Because the plugin is only reachable by calling it explicitly, which the project never does, the function is unreachable, with moderate confidence given the uncached Pillow source.

The vulnerable function sits on cryptography's RSA encryption and decryption path, which is exercised only when a program encrypts or decrypts data with an RSA key. This project pulls cryptography in only indirectly through its certificate parsing and SSH libraries and never performs an RSA encryption or decryption operation itself, since its TLS scanning only reads and inspects certificates. Because no RSA encrypt or decrypt call is ever made, the vulnerable function is unreachable.

The vulnerable function serializes a private key and certificates into a PKCS12 bundle and runs only when a program calls cryptography's PKCS12 serialization API. This project only reads and inspects server certificates during TLS scanning and never assembles or exports a PKCS12 bundle. With no call to the serialization API, the vulnerable function is unreachable.

The vulnerable functions live in aiohttp's pure-Python HTTP response parser, which the client uses to read status lines and headers from every response it receives. This project drives aiohttp purely as a client in its HTTP scanning engine, so it does exercise response parsing, but the shipped installation includes the compiled C parser extension that shadows this pure-Python code unless the AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS environment variable is set. The vulnerable functions are therefore reachable only when that extension is disabled, and I label the row reachable under that condition.

The vulnerable function belongs to pyOpenSSL's SSL connection module, which wraps live TLS connections and installs a server-name callback. This project imports pyOpenSSL only for its certificate-parsing helpers in the crypto module and performs its actual TLS handshakes with the Python standard library ssl module, never touching the pyOpenSSL SSL module. Because the SSL connection module is never used, the vulnerable function is unreachable.

The vulnerable function is a constructor within pyOpenSSL's SSL connection module used to set up TLS contexts and connections. This project uses pyOpenSSL exclusively through its crypto module to load and inspect certificates and creates its TLS sockets with the Python standard library ssl module instead. Because it never constructs a pyOpenSSL SSL object, the vulnerable function is unreachable.

The vulnerable functions belong to aiohttp's connector DNS cache table, which the default TCP connector constructs and populates whenever a client session resolves hostnames. This project creates a ClientSession with no explicit connector for its HTTP scanning, so aiohttp builds the default TCP connector and its DNS cache table, and each outbound probe against a hostname adds entries to it. Because the scanner issues many real outbound requests through this session, the vulnerable functions are reachable.

The vulnerable function belongs to aiohttp's multipart form builder and runs only when a program constructs a FormData object and adds fields to it. This project never builds an aiohttp FormData anywhere in its scanning modules; the modules that send request bodies pass them through plain json or data request options instead. Because no FormData is ever created, the vulnerable function has no call path and is unreachable.

The vulnerable function is the static-file handler of aiohttp's server-side URL dispatcher and runs only inside a running aiohttp web application that has registered a static route. This project exposes its own web interface through Flask and uses aiohttp exclusively as an outbound HTTP client, so it never starts an aiohttp web server or registers any routes. With no aiohttp server present, the vulnerable function is unreachable.

The vulnerable functions belong to aiohttp's multipart reader and the readuntil helper it uses to split MIME headers, reached only when a program parses a multipart response. This project reads every response body with a plain content.read() call and never invokes multipart parsing or the readuntil primitive. Because the scanner never parses multipart data, none of these functions are on any executed path and the row is unreachable.

The vulnerable function is the server-side request-body parser of aiohttp's web request object and executes only when an aiohttp web server handles an incoming request. This project serves its web interface with Flask and uses aiohttp only to send outbound client requests, so it never constructs or processes an aiohttp server request. The vulnerable function is therefore unreachable.

The vulnerable function is the core request-dispatch method through which every aiohttp client call is routed, whatever verb is used. This project resolves the HTTP method by name on its client session and invokes it for each scan step, and all of those calls funnel through this single dispatch method. Because the scanner issues many outbound requests this way, the vulnerable function is reachable.

This cluster mixes a server-side response method, which this client-only project never reaches, with the pure-Python routine that serializes outgoing request headers when the client sends a request. The scanner does send client requests and therefore serializes request headers, but the installed compiled writer extension shadows this pure-Python serializer unless AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS is set. The row is reachable only under that no-extensions condition, so I label it reachable with reduced confidence.

The vulnerable functions are the pure-Python header-parsing routines aiohttp uses when a client reads response headers. This project reads a response for every scan probe, so it does drive header parsing, but the shipped compiled parser extension shadows the pure-Python implementation unless AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS is enabled. The vulnerable functions are reachable only under that condition, so the row is labeled reachable with medium confidence.

The vulnerable functions persist and reload aiohttp's cookie jar to and from a file and run only when a program explicitly calls save or load with a path. This project never persists a cookie jar and does not invoke either method anywhere in its code. With no call to the persistence routines, the vulnerable functions are unreachable.

The vulnerable functions are the constructor and signing routine of paramiko's RSA key class. This project's SSH brute-force library connects to target servers with password or no-auth strategies, and during the key-exchange handshake paramiko parses the server's host key and constructs an RSA key object whenever the server presents an RSA host key, which reaches the constructor before authentication even completes; the signing routine, used only for client public-key authentication, is not reached under password brute force. Because RSA host keys are common and the constructor is entered during the handshake against such servers, the row is reachable, though I set medium confidence because it depends on the target's host-key type and paramiko's source was not available to trace every edge.

The vulnerable function is again aiohttp's central client request-dispatch method, which handles every outbound request regardless of verb. This project routes all of its scanning requests through a client session method resolved by name, and each of those calls passes through this dispatch method. Because the scanner makes many such requests, the vulnerable function is reachable.

The vulnerable function is the payload headers property that aiohttp reads when it copies a body payload's content-type and related headers onto an outgoing request. This project sends request bodies through the json and data options in several scanning modules, and aiohttp builds a payload and reads its headers whenever such a body is present. Because those body-carrying requests are part of live scan modules, the vulnerable function is reachable.

This cluster contains server-side protocol code that this client-only project never runs, alongside the pure-Python response-parser routines aiohttp uses to feed and length-check incoming client data. The scanner reads a response for each probe and would drive those parser routines, but the compiled parser extension shadows them unless AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS is set. The parser members are reachable only under that no-extensions condition, so the row is reachable with medium confidence.

The vulnerable functions belong to aiohttp's WebSocket frame reader and run only when a program opens an aiohttp WebSocket connection. This project uses aiohttp solely for HTTP requests and never calls the WebSocket client API, so the WebSocket reader is never entered regardless of whether the compiled extension is active. The vulnerable functions are therefore unreachable.

The vulnerable function is the call handler of aiohttp's digest-authentication client middleware and runs only when that middleware is explicitly attached to a session. This project constructs its client session with no middleware and configures no digest authentication anywhere. Because the middleware is never instantiated, the vulnerable function is unreachable.

The vulnerable function is the low-level buffer read of aiohttp's stream reader, invoked by the client's read and readany body-reading routines. This project reads every response body by calling read on the response content stream, which passes directly into this routine. Because this stream reader is pure Python with no compiled shadow and the scanner reads a body for every request, the vulnerable function is reachable.

The vulnerable functions serialize and reload aiohttp's cookie jar from disk and execute only on an explicit save or load call. This project never persists or restores a cookie jar and invokes neither routine. With no persistence call in the code, the vulnerable functions are unreachable.

The vulnerable function finalizes an aiohttp server-side streaming response and runs only inside a running aiohttp web application. This project serves its web interface with Flask and uses aiohttp only as an outbound client, so it never constructs or writes an aiohttp server response. The vulnerable function is unreachable.

The vulnerable function torch.serialization.persistent_load is an unpickler callback that only runs inside torch.load, so it is reached only when the project deserializes a checkpoint. This project uses torch purely for tensor operations and never calls torch.load, torch.jit.load or load_state_dict anywhere in its own code; its default configuration disables VAD, selects sherpa_onnx (an ONNX runtime) for ASR and edge_tts for TTS, and the backends that would deserialize torch checkpoints (funasr, coqui) are optional and absent from the requirements. No valid call path to the vulnerable function exists in the project as configured, although a user who installed one of the optional torch-based backends could create one.

The vulnerable function google.protobuf.json_format._Parser._ConvertAnyMessage belongs to protobuf's JSON parsing layer and is reached only through google.protobuf.json_format.Parse. Protobuf is present only as a transitive dependency of onnxruntime, and the project uses onnxruntime solely to query execution providers and run inference through its C++ bindings in the sherpa_onnx ASR backend; no project code imports google.protobuf.json_format. The ONNX inference path never parses protobuf JSON, so no valid call path to the vulnerable function exists.

The vulnerable functions aiohttp.http_parser.HttpParser.__init__ and aiohttp.http_parser.HeadersParser.parse_headers belong to aiohttp's pure-Python HTTP parsing pipeline. This project uses aiohttp only as an HTTP client, creating a ClientSession for the BiliBili live platform and for the proxy handler, and every client response is parsed by ResponseHandler through HttpResponseParser, which does reach these functions. However, aiohttp rebinds the parser classes to its compiled C implementation at import time unless AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS is set, so the vulnerable functions are reached on every client response only when the application runs with AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS set; the default installation shadows them with the C extension.

The reported path contains a fabricated cross-library constructor edge: requests.adapters.BaseAdapter.__init__ does not create or invoke python_multipart.multipart.File. The vulnerable function python_multipart.multipart.File.__init__ is instantiated only by python_multipart's high-level FormParser, which is used by parse_form. The project does expose a multipart upload endpoint whose form data is parsed by Starlette, but starlette.formparsers.MultiPartParser drives python-multipart through its low-level MultipartParser and callback interface and never constructs the high-level File object, so no valid call path to the vulnerable function exists.

The vulnerable function requests.utils.extract_zipped_paths is part of requests' certificate handling and is invoked from HTTPAdapter.cert_verify whenever an HTTPS request is sent. The project's ASR helper download_and_extract calls requests.get, which flows through requests.sessions.Session.request and Session.send into requests.adapters.HTTPAdapter.send and then cert_verify. The vulnerable function is therefore reached on every model download the ASR utility performs, so a valid call path exists.

The vulnerable functions dotenv.main.rewrite, dotenv.main.set_key and dotenv.main.unset_key belong to python-dotenv's file-writing API; rewrite is called only from set_key and unset_key, which back the dotenv set and dotenv unset commands. The project never imports dotenv itself, and python-dotenv is present only transitively through mcp and pydantic-settings, both of which use only the read-side APIs load_dotenv and dotenv_values. Nothing reachable from the project calls the write API, so no valid call path to any of the vulnerable functions exists.

The vulnerable functions aiohttp.connector._DNSCacheTable.__init__ and _DNSCacheTable.add belong to aiohttp's client connector, which builds its DNS cache table when a TCPConnector is created. This project constructs an aiohttp ClientSession in both the BiliBili live platform and the proxy handler, and aiohttp.client.ClientSession.__init__ unconditionally creates a TCPConnector, whose constructor instantiates _DNSCacheTable. The vulnerable code is therefore reached on every client session the project creates, with no gating condition, so a valid call path exists.

The vulnerable function aiohttp.formdata.FormData.add_field is reached only when a client request carries a multipart or urlencoded form body built through aiohttp's FormData helper. This project never constructs a FormData object and issues only bodyless GET requests and WebSocket upgrades through its aiohttp client, and aiohttp.client_reqrep.ClientRequest.update_body_from_data returns immediately when the body is None. No valid call path to the vulnerable function exists.

The vulnerable function aiohttp.web_urldispatcher.StaticResource._handle belongs to the aiohttp.web server's static file router. This project uses aiohttp strictly as an HTTP client and never imports aiohttp.web or configures an aiohttp web router; its HTTP server is FastAPI/Starlette served by Uvicorn. Since no aiohttp StaticResource is ever created, no valid call path to the vulnerable function exists.

The vulnerable functions aiohttp.multipart.MultipartReader.__init__, MultipartReader._read_headers and aiohttp.streams.StreamReader.readuntil belong to aiohttp's multipart response parsing pipeline, where _read_headers drives StreamReader.readuntil. This project never calls response.multipart() on an aiohttp client response and never calls readuntil or readline directly; it consumes responses only through read() and json(). No valid call path to any of the vulnerable functions exists.

The vulnerable function aiohttp.web_request.BaseRequest.post is the form parser of the aiohttp.web server and is reached only when an aiohttp web handler reads an incoming request body. This project uses aiohttp as a client only and never imports aiohttp.web, so no aiohttp server request object is ever created. No valid call path to the vulnerable function exists.

The vulnerable function aiohttp.client.ClientSession._request is the central dispatch method of aiohttp's client, reached by every request or WebSocket handshake made through a ClientSession. This project calls session.get() from the blivedm BiliBili live client and calls ws_connect from the proxy handler, and ws_connect flows through ClientSession._ws_connect into _request. The vulnerable function is therefore reached on every live-platform and proxy request the project makes, so a valid call path exists.

Of the reported root causes, aiohttp.web_response.StreamResponse._set_status belongs to the aiohttp.web server, which this project does not use, but aiohttp.http_writer._py_serialize_headers is on the client path: aiohttp.client_reqrep.ClientRequest hands its headers to http_writer's _serialize_headers when writing a request. The project does issue aiohttp client requests, so that pure-Python serializer would be reached, except that aiohttp rebinds _serialize_headers to its compiled C implementation at import time unless AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS is set. The vulnerable function is therefore reached on every outbound client request, but only when the application runs with AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS set.

The vulnerable functions aiohttp.http_parser.HeadersParser.parse_headers and aiohttp.http_parser.HttpParser.parse_headers belong to aiohttp's pure-Python header parser, which is driven by HttpResponseParser on the client response path this project exercises through its aiohttp ClientSession. As with the other http_parser findings, aiohttp swaps the pure-Python parser for its compiled C extension at import time unless AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS is set. The vulnerable functions are therefore reached on every client response, but only when the application runs with AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS set.

The vulnerable functions aiohttp.cookiejar.CookieJar.save and CookieJar.load implement cookie persistence, pickling the jar to and from disk, and both require an explicit file path supplied by the caller. This project only calls cookie_jar.update_cookies on the session's jar when setting up the BiliBili live client, and never calls save or load anywhere. No valid call path to either vulnerable function exists.

The vulnerable function aiohttp.client.ClientSession._request is the central dispatch method of aiohttp's HTTP client, reached by every request and WebSocket handshake issued through a ClientSession. This project reaches it through the blivedm live client's session.get() calls and through the proxy handler's ws_connect, which routes through ClientSession._ws_connect into _request. The vulnerable function is therefore reached on every outbound aiohttp request the project makes, so a valid call path exists.

The vulnerable function jwt.api_jws.PyJWS._load is reached only through jwt.decode when a JWT is verified. PyJWT is present only as a transitive dependency of mcp, where jwt is imported solely in the OAuth client-credentials extension of the MCP client's auth layer, and this project's MCP client is configured with the stdio transport and no auth provider. The project itself never imports jwt, so jwt.decode is never invoked and no valid call path to the vulnerable function exists.

The reported path contains a fabricated cross-library constructor edge, since requests.adapters.BaseAdapter.__init__ does not create a starlette.datastructures.URL; the vulnerable function is instead reached through the project's own server pipeline. This project serves a FastAPI/Starlette application, and starlette.datastructures.URL.__init__ is constructed on ordinary request paths, both by the Starlette Router's slash-redirect handling (redirect_slashes defaults to True) and by StaticFiles' html-mode redirect, which the project enables by mounting static directories with html=True. The vulnerable function is therefore reached on normal incoming requests, so a valid call path exists.

The vulnerable function starlette.staticfiles.StaticFiles.get_response is the method that resolves and returns a file for every request handled by a Starlette StaticFiles mount. This project defines CORSStaticFiles and AvatarStaticFiles as subclasses of StaticFiles whose own get_response overrides delegate to super().get_response, and it mounts them at /cache, /live2d-models, /bg, /avatars, /web-tool and the site root. Any request for a static asset invokes the vulnerable function, so a valid call path exists.

The vulnerable function is the headers property of aiohttp.payload.Payload, which is only exercised once a Payload object has been created for a client request body. This project issues only bodyless requests and WebSocket upgrades through its aiohttp client, and aiohttp.client_reqrep.ClientRequest.update_body_from_data returns immediately when the body is None, so no Payload is ever constructed. No valid call path to the vulnerable function exists.

Of the reported root causes, aiohttp.web_protocol.__init__ belongs to the aiohttp.web server, which this project does not use, and the http_parser sinks are shadowed by aiohttp's compiled C extension, but aiohttp.base_protocol.BaseProtocol.resume_reading is reachable on the client path. The project's aiohttp client responses are handled by ResponseHandler, which extends BaseProtocol and calls resume_reading as part of ordinary transport flow control. The vulnerable function is reached on every client response the project reads, with no gating condition, so a valid call path exists.

The vulnerable functions aiohttp._websocket.reader_py._handle_frame and _feed_data belong to aiohttp's pure-Python WebSocket frame reader. This project does open a client WebSocket through the proxy handler's ws_connect and pumps frames through its forwarding loop over server_ws.receive(), which feeds data into the WebSocketReader. However, aiohttp selects the Cython reader_c implementation at import time unless AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS is set, so the vulnerable functions are reached on every proxied WebSocket frame only when the application runs with AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS set.

The vulnerable function is the __call__ method of aiohttp.client_middleware_digest_auth.DigestAuthMiddleware, which runs only when a digest-auth middleware is attached to a client session. This project constructs its ClientSession without passing any middlewares, so the session's middleware tuple stays at its empty default and aiohttp only invokes the middleware chain when that tuple is non-empty. Digest authentication is never configured, so no valid call path to the vulnerable function exists.

The vulnerable function aiohttp.streams.StreamReader._read_nowait is the internal buffer drain used by StreamReader.read when a client reads a response body. This project shares an aiohttp ClientSession with the blivedm live client, which issues session.get() requests against the BiliBili API and reads their response bodies in the normal way, so StreamReader.read returns through _read_nowait. The vulnerable function is reached whenever the live client consumes a response body, so a valid call path exists, assuming blivedm reads the bodies of the responses it fetches, which is its standard behaviour.

The vulnerable functions aiohttp.cookiejar.CookieJar.save and CookieJar._load_json_data implement cookie persistence to and from disk and are only reached when the caller passes an explicit file path to save or load. This project only calls cookie_jar.update_cookies on the session's jar when setting up the BiliBili live client and never persists or reloads cookies. No valid call path to either vulnerable function exists.

The vulnerable function aiohttp.web_response.StreamResponse.write_eof belongs to the aiohttp.web server's response API and is reached only when an aiohttp web handler finishes writing a response. This project uses aiohttp strictly as an HTTP client and never imports aiohttp.web; its web layer is FastAPI/Starlette. No aiohttp server response object is ever created, so no valid call path to the vulnerable function exists.

The vulnerable function pytest.tmpdir.getbasetemp is only reachable through pytest's test runner. Horizon uses pytest exclusively under the tests directory; none of its production CLI, webhook, wizard, or MCP entry points invoke pytest or getbasetemp. Therefore, no production call path reaches the accepted VF.

The vulnerable xmltodict functions _has_angle_brackets and _emit are not invoked by Horizon. xmltodict is present transitively through the optional OpenBB SEC extension, but Horizon only calls obb.news.company and contains no SEC filing or XML serialization path. Therefore, no project entry point reaches either accepted VF.

Horizon has a production Gemini configuration path that constructs google.genai.Client and calls await self.client.aio.models.generate_content from GeminiClient.complete. google-genai 1.64.0 uses aiohttp for its asynchronous HTTP transport. When the Gemini endpoint returns an HTTP response, aiohttp's ResponseHandler creates an HttpResponseParser, invoking the accepted HttpParser.__init__ VF, and feeds the response bytes through HttpResponseParser.parse_message and HttpParser.parse_headers into the accepted HeadersParser.parse_headers VF. Therefore, an enabled Gemini provider provides a production call path from Horizon to the accepted root-cause functions.

Horizon uses python-dotenv only through load_dotenv in its CLI, setup wizard, webhook CLI, and MCP adapter. It never imports or calls rewrite, set_key, or unset_key, and no production path modifies an environment file through python-dotenv. Therefore, none of the accepted VFs are reachable.

Horizon does not parse BER/ASN.1 input or call pyasn1 decoding APIs. Its Google GenAI integration constructs genai.Client with an API key rather than using a service-account or certificate-decoding flow. Although pyasn1 is present transitively through google-auth and rsa, no production path reaches pyasn1.codec.ber.decoder.__call__.

Horizon provides a production Gemini path that constructs google.genai.Client and calls await self.client.aio.models.generate_content. google-genai's asynchronous transport creates an aiohttp ClientSession, whose default TCPConnector directly instantiates _DNSCacheTable, reaching the accepted _DNSCacheTable.__init__ VF. When the client connects to the Gemini API hostname, TCPConnector resolves the host and stores the resolved addresses through _DNSCacheTable.add. Therefore, both accepted root-cause functions are reachable when Gemini is configured as an AI provider or selected through the provider fallback chain.

Horizon does not construct aiohttp FormData or submit multipart form fields. Its native HTTP integrations use httpx, while the optional OpenBB path only invokes obb.news.company for news retrieval. No reachable operation calls aiohttp.FormData.add_field, so the accepted VF is unreachable.

aiohttp.web.StaticResource._handle belongs to aiohttp's server-side static-file handler. Horizon does not create an aiohttp web.Application, register static resources, or run an aiohttp HTTP server. Its MCP entry runs over stdio. Therefore, no production request path reaches the accepted VF.

The accepted VFs belong to aiohttp multipart-stream processing. Horizon does not instantiate MultipartReader, parse multipart bodies, or expose an aiohttp upload endpoint. The optional OpenBB news operation consumes structured provider results rather than multipart data, so no production path reaches MultipartReader.__init__, MultipartReader._read_headers, or the associated StreamReader.readuntil path.

aiohttp.web_request.BaseRequest.post is a server-side API used to parse POST form bodies. Horizon does not run an aiohttp web server or define aiohttp request handlers, and its MCP server uses stdio rather than an aiohttp HTTP endpoint. Therefore, the accepted VF is unreachable.

Horizon provides a production Gemini execution path that constructs google.genai.Client and invokes await self.client.aio.models.generate_content from GeminiClient.complete. The google-genai asynchronous API client sends the generated-content HTTP request through its aiohttp transport, whose ClientSession.request method directly invokes the accepted ClientSession._request root-cause function. The construction is unconditional on every adapter created by a requests Session, so the vulnerable functions are reached on every currency-conversion request the project makes. The tier tool's claimed path through werkzeug._internal._ColorStreamHandler.__init__ into PoolManager.__init__ is a fabricated cross-library constructor edge, but the real path through requests is valid and sufficient.

This project runs as a Flask application under CPython on a normal server platform, so the Emscripten contrib module is never loaded and the vulnerable function is dead code; no valid call path to it exists.

The static folder exists and the routes are registered on the application, so the vulnerable function is reached on every request that serves the favicon or a static asset.

The vulnerable function, urllib3.response.MultiDecoder.__init__, belongs to urllib3's response content-decoding pipeline and is constructed by HTTPResponse._get_decoder whenever the response carries a comma-separated, multi-value Content-Encoding header. This project calls requests.get(...).json() in ihatemoney.currency_convertor, and requests.models.Response.content drives iter_content, which streams the raw urllib3 response with decode_content enabled; that reaches HTTPResponse.read and its _init_decoder step. The vulnerable function is therefore reached on any exchange-rate response whose server returns a chained Content-Encoding value, which is the only gating condition. The tier tool's claimed path from werkzeug._internal._ColorStreamHandler.__init__ into MultiDecoder.__init__ is a fabricated cross-library constructor edge, but the genuine requests-to-urllib3 path stands on its own.
